questions.question: When power is shared among different organs of government, then it known as _____.
questions.solution: Sharing of power between different organs of the government is known as separation of powers. As per Indian constitution, power is distributed between the executive, the judiciary and the legislative.

questions.question: Which type of government is based on free and fair election where those currently in power have a fair chance of losing?
questions.solution: It is the democratic form of government that allows for free and fair election and a government has equal chance of winning or losing as that of other political parties. In other form of government, there is no such system of free and fair election.

questions.question: For how much time the Presidents Rule can be extended in India with the approval of Parliament in every six months?
questions.solution: President Rule under article 356 of the constitution can be extended for a maximum of three years with repeated parliamentary approval every six months. Initially, it is imposed for a period of six months.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of members required to be present in any one of the two houses of parliament for its functioning?
questions.solution: The minimum number of members required to be present in any two house of the parliament for its functioning is known as Quorum of the parliament, which is 10% of the total members of that house. This is envisaged in Article 100 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is CORRECT about coalition form of government?

options.text: Sharing of power at different levels
Sharing of power by different social groups
Sharing of power by two or more political parties

questions.solution:
A coalition government is a type of government where two or more political parties join together in parliament/ assembly to run the government and agree on a policy program.

 
• A coalition government is a cabinet of a parliamentary government in which several parties cooperate.
 
• The usual reason given for this arrangement is that no party on its own can achieve a majority in the parliament.
 
• A coalition government might also be created in a time of national difficulty or crisis, for example during wartime, to give a government the high degree of perceived political legitimacy it desires and also playing a role in diminishing internal political strife.
 
• In such times, parties have formed all-party coalitions (national unity governments, grand coalitions).
 
• If a coalition collapses a confidence vote is held or a motion of no confidence is taken.
 
• A coalition government is oftentimes considered a very weak form of government because there is no majority party.

Thus, we can say that a **coalition form of government means Sharing of power by two or more political parties.**

questions.question: Jet engine works on the principal of conservation of ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Jet engine works on the phenomenon of Conservation of Linear Momentum__.
 
• It produces a large volume of gases through the combustion of fuel, which is allowed to escape in backward direction through a jet.
 
• The backward rushing gas gains large momentum because of high velocity.
 
• It thus imparts an equal and opposite momentum to the jet engine.
 
• The jet engine, thus, moves forward with high speed.
 
• Conservation of Linear Momentum states that a body in motion retains its total momentum (product of mass and vector velocity) unless an external force is applied to it.

questions.question: What will happen to the level of water in a vessel when a piece of ice floating in it melts?
questions.solution:
It will remain same and this phenomenon is explained by Archimedes Principle.

A floating object displaces an amount of water equal to its own weight. Since water expands when it freezes, one unit (of weight) of frozen water has a larger volume than one unit of liquid water. A completely submerged ice cube weighing one unit displaces more than one unit of liquid water. The cube will rise until the volume remaining under the surface displaces only one unit of water.

questions.question: Which of the following quantity is a measure of inertia?
questions.solution:
The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion is dependent upon its mass. Inertia is a quantity which is solely dependent upon mass. The more mass an object has, the more inertia it has, the more tendency it has to resist changes in its state of motion.

E.g. A truck has a heavy mass so it becomes hard to apply brakes suddenly to change its state.

questions.question: Which among the following types of trees is also called as sun-loving plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heliophytes.**__

**Heliophytes**, also** called sun-loving plants, are those that require full exposure to the sun for their optimum **growth.

E.g. Sugar Cane.

 
• Xerophytes: Those plants which have adaptations to survive in an area with less water. eg: cactus
 
• Saprophytes: Those plants which get energy from dead and decaying matter. Eg: Mushroom.
 
• Halophytes: Salt tolerant plants, that grow in areas with high salinity. Eg: mangroves
